newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open weaker after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open weaker after jobs data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills open mostly weaker on Friday after the release of July jobs data, amid a softer currency, some rate hike speculation and weakness in the U.S. market

"Even though we are a little bit weaker we've done very well in our market in the face of everything else," said one T-bill trader with a brokerage. "The market was short, got shorter last evening ahead of this number today. Now the feeling is they're not going (to hike) and they're covering."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill softened to yield 3.36 percent from 3.35 percent at Thursday's close.

Statistics Canada on Friday reported that the unemployment rate fell to 9.0 percent in July from 9.1 percent in June and employment rose by 15,000. However, analysts noted most of the jobs were part time and full-time employment actually declined in June.
The report was weaker-than-expected and dollar weakened past C$1.3900 (US$0.7194) in the wake of its release.

Dealers said the report did not provide enough strength to prompt an immediate Bank of Canada rate hike. At the same time, analysts said further weakness in the Canadian dollar could force a Bank of Canada tightening.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.76 percent from 3.75 percent on Thursday. The one-year when-issued T-bill traded unchanged to yield 4.27 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.30 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
